taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Regional Texas treatments may use Passiflora lutea var. glabriflora; the learner remains species-level.
look_here_first: LOOK for a broad shallow 3-lobed LEAF with entire margins, then check the PETIOLE: no glands. Flip the leaf underside: no extra-floral nectar dots; P. affinis has underside nectar dots and floral bracts (both have glandless petioles). At flower base P. lutea lacks floral bracts and small flowers are <25 mm across with straight thin unclubbed corona filaments.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center's Purola Preserve natural flora lists Passiflora lutea among plants occurring naturally and not introduced. Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Passifloraceae herbarium index includes Passiflora lutea. Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a field-based treatment of Passiflora lutea var. glabriflora within the local flora.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Cultivated vines and garden escapes are not used as native-county evidence.

best_field_traits: perennial climbing or trailing vine with axillary tendrils
petioles eglandular — no paired extrafloral nectary bumps
leaf blades shallowly to moderately 3-lobed, usually wider than long
lobes broad and rounded to obtuse; margins entire rather than serrate
fine veins prominently raised on the lower leaf surface
flowers small and inconspicuous, roughly 2–2.5 cm across in regional material
sepals green; petals pale green-yellow; corona pale green/white to yellow
ripe berries small, purple-black, roughly 8–15 mm
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Passiflora tenuiloba: P. tenuiloba has petiole glands and very narrow, deeply divided 3–9-lobed 'birdwing' leaves; P. lutea has glandless petioles and broad rounded 3-lobed leaves. Passiflora incarnata: P. incarnata has two conspicuous petiole glands, deeply 3-lobed serrate leaves, much larger flowers, and large maypop fruits. P. lutea has glandless petioles, entire leaf margins and tiny flowers/fruits.

comparisons.key_distinctions: P. tenuiloba has petiole glands and very narrow, deeply divided 3–9-lobed 'birdwing' leaves; P. lutea has glandless petioles and broad rounded 3-lobed leaves. P. incarnata has two conspicuous petiole glands, deeply 3-lobed serrate leaves, much larger flowers, and large maypop fruits. P. lutea has glandless petioles, entire leaf margins and tiny flowers/fruits.
